title: Reproduction in Plants and Animals
seo_title: Year 5 Science: Reproduction in Plants and Animals Worksheets (Flowers, Pollination, Seeds)
standard_code: Year 5: Living things and their habitats
standard_text: Describe the life process of reproduction in some plants and animals.
meta_desc: Free Year 5 science worksheets on reproduction in plants and animals: sexual and asexual reproduction, parts of a flower, pollination, fertilisation and seed dispersal. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Two parents or one: new life begins.
key_sub: Flowers are pollinated and fertilised to make seeds; runners and bulbs make copies.
body_html:
How to think about it

Plants and animals reproduce to make new living things of the same kind.

  • Sexual reproduction needs two parents; offspring vary. Asexual reproduction needs one parent; offspring are identical (runners, bulbs, tubers, cuttings).
  • In a flower, the anther makes pollen and the stigma catches it. Pollination → fertilisation → seed and fruit.
  • Seeds are dispersed by wind, animals, water or by bursting pods.
Example

Strawberry runner: how many parents?

The new plant grows from one plant

Answer: one: asexual

Example

Burdock seeds have hooks. Dispersed how?

Hooks catch on fur

Answer: by animals

Common mistakes

  • Mixing up pollination and fertilisation.
  • Thinking petals make the pollen.
  • Thinking all seeds are spread by the wind.

faq.q: What is the difference between sexual and asexual reproduction?
faq.a: Sexual reproduction needs two parents and the offspring vary. Asexual reproduction needs one parent and the offspring are identical to it.

faq.q: What is the difference between pollination and fertilisation?
faq.a: Pollination is pollen moving from an anther to a stigma. Fertilisation happens later, when the pollen joins with an ovule in the ovary to start a seed.
By the wind (dandelion, sycamore), by animals (burdock hooks, berries that are eaten), by water (coconut) or by pods bursting open (peas, gorse).

items.q: Garlic cloves are planted to grow new garlic. Which kind of asexual reproduction is this?
items.e: Asexual reproduction needs only one parent; the new plant is identical to it.

items.q: "The bee carries the pollen to another flower of the same kind." What happens next?
c: The seeds are dispersed and can grow into new plants.
Pollen lands on the sticky stigma (pollination).
A bee visits a flower and pollen sticks to its body.
The pollen joins with an ovule in the ovary (fertilisation).
items.e: Pollination → fertilisation → seed and fruit → dispersal.
